props.title: One voice and a guitar, or the guitar alone.
props.lede: Sung, it’s one voice and a guitar working blues, roots and the singer-songwriter catalog, and a cocktail hour or a patio takes a voice well. Instrumental, it’s jazz standards and Spanish-tinged sets, which sit easiest under dinner conversation. The nylon-string version is the Spanish guitarist, and the sung version has its own page as the singer and guitarist.

props.html: One musician with a small sound system fits where a band can’t: a private dining space at a restaurant, a gallery evening set between the works, a house where nobody wants the furniture moved. When the guest list outgrows one instrument, the acoustic duo and the jazz duo are the next sizes up. The covers list is on the repertoire page.

items.q: How much space and power does a solo guitarist need?
items.a: A corner of about 6 by 4 feet, one dedicated 20-amp circuit, 45 minutes to set up and 30 to pack down. The circuit should be one the caterer isn't also using, which is the detail most often missed. Sound support that's the right size for the venue comes with the booking.

items.q: Is one guitarist enough for a cocktail hour?
items.a: For a shorter guest list, yes. One guitar sounds like live music from anywhere in the space and stays under the conversation, and the nearest table carries on talking over it. When the crowd is big enough that one instrument disappears into it, the duo is the next size up.
A working guitarist from our roster, matched to the set you want, sung or instrumental. We name them to you when the contract is written.

items.q: Can we ask for a song?
items.a: Yes. Send a do-not-play list or build the set with us, and the guitarist learns one song of your choosing as part of every booking. If the night runs long, another half hour is easy to add on the night.

items.q: Can the solo guitarist play outdoors?
items.a: Yes, and patios and courtyards are regular work. It needs a covered, level and dry spot with power run to it, and we agree a plan for moving indoors with you ahead of time, because Colorado evenings turn cold fast.
